title: An AI-generated influencer entered Alabama 'RushTok' - Some fans didn't care that she was fake
key_facts: Olivia Moore, investment partner at venture firm Andreessen Horowitz, created an AI influencer named Janie B who posted TikTok videos during University of Alabama sorority rush ('RushTok')
Her first video, posted 8 Aug 2026, has over 120,000 views; she spent about $100 in credits for a week of videos
Moore built Janie with ChatGPT for the image and prompts and MiniMax H3 for video
Viewers under about 25 spotted the AI quickly; older viewers were often fooled; by day two or three the audience largely knew, and some said they did not care
TikTok initially flagged 8 of 20 videos as AI-generated; 16 of 20 now carry a label
Moore says humans are currently getting better at detecting AI faster than AI improves, and that reactions turned positive once she revealed the experiment
The Alabama Panhellenic Association declined to comment
quote_evidence: Every detail of every video on Janie's account, from her dorm room, to her outfits, to Janie herself, was generated by artificial intelligence.
Of the 20 AI-generated videos she uploaded, Moore said TikTok only initially flagged 8 as containing AI-generated media.
"I would say anyone under maybe 25 immediately clocked her as AI," Moore said.
why_it_matters_hint: A $100 AI persona passed as a real college student for a day, and TikTok's labels caught less than half at first
event_date: 8 Aug 2026 onward (rush week); interview published 3 Oct 2026
notes: Fox News Digital interview with Moore; the detection figures are her own account. Event is from August, re-reported now.
